page.layout: One page of text in one column: a short introductory paragraph, then a chronological table of years with consul names in braces, followed by prose lines between the table rows. Running head at top. Catchword at bottom right. No printed margin notes; only a few small dot marks at the left of the table.

main_text.p: Ut autem lectori id ipsum evidentius & quasi ad oculum pateat, sequentem, quam subjicio, tabellam inspiciat velim.
main_text.l: An. ÆRÆ Vulg. | Vere. | Jul. per Jul. | U. C.
main_text.p: Augustus die Aug. xix. mortuus, Tiberium habuit in imperio Successorem.
Tiberius annum egit 1 & 2 atque etiamnum Annius Rufus Procurator Judææ fuit.

Tiberius annum egit 2 & 3.
Valerius Gratus mittitur in locum Annii. Ann. 1.

Tiberius 3 & 4 anno præfuit.
Valerii Grati annus 2 est.

page.notes: Small dot marks stand to the left of the first year row and beside the consul line for 770 (possibly printer's marks or reference marks; no matching note on the page). A printer's dot also stands at the top of the page above the running head; it is an ornament and is left out. "Valerii Gratu ... 3." : the word may read "Grati"; marked [?]. The table braces are rendered as " | coss." after each pair of consuls. The last line "Tibe-" is the catchword and is printed once in bottom_margin; the duplicate in main_text should be treated as the catchword only.
